why: A class's methods are those of the one class definition its name resolves to, and of its superclasses, each resolved the same way (MATLAB doc 'Class Precedence and MATLAB Path': of same-named classes the first on the path is the class; 'Function Precedence Order'). `addpath` puts a folder at the front of the path, so after `addpath('lib'); addpath('tools')` the superclass `Mid` of `app/Widget.m` is `tools/Mid.m`, which has no `go`, and `w.go()` reaches no method, nor does `m.go()` on an object of `Mid` itself: another copy's `Mid::go` in `lib/Mid.m` is another class's. With the order swapped, `Mid` is `lib/Mid.m` and `w.go()` calls its `go`; with `tools/Mid.m` deleted too; with it back, nothing again. Each step must end where a fresh index ends (project rule; the step 15 review's fixture, N1).
